title: Replace the spark plug
summary: Swap a worn plug to fix hard starts, misfires and poor fuel economy.
parts: Spark plug (type from your owner's manual)

steps.text: Work on a cold engine. Remove any covers or panels to reach the plug cap.
steps.caution: Aluminum cylinder heads strip easily when hot. Let the engine cool fully.

steps.text: Pull the plug cap straight off by the cap, not the wire.
Blow or brush debris away from around the plug so nothing falls into the cylinder.
Unscrew the old plug with the socket. Check its tip: light tan is healthy; black, oily or white means it needs a closer look.
Check the gap on the new plug and adjust only if it is outside the spec in your manual.
Thread the new plug in by hand until it seats, then tighten it to the torque on your spec sheet.
steps.caution: Starting the plug with a wrench can cross-thread it. Always start by hand.

steps.text: Push the cap on until it clicks, refit the covers and start the engine.
